title: Go SDK for ZIdentity (ziam services): name lookups, write models and where its paths depart from the contract

prose.text: The Go SDK reaches ZIdentity through the `zscaler/ziam/services` packages; their functions and endpoints are generated (`node scripts/kb.mjs surface zid`). Behavior shared by every Go product, retries and error decoding included, is in [[shared.sdk-go.retries]] and [[shared.sdk-go.request-handling]].

groups-update-panics.statement: So a group update whose PUT answers with no body panics the calling process after the update has been applied, instead of returning the nil result the users and API-client updates return.
groups-update-panics.conditions: Follows from Go evaluating `updatedGroup.ID` on a nil pointer, the failure the users package's comment describes for its own function; whether the groups PUT ever answers without a body is not observed.

admin-scope-optional.statement: The Go SDK's comment says an administrative entitlement for the ZIAM service carries no `scope` key at all, and the Go model holds `Scope` and `Service` as pointers because as value types the absence could not be told apart from `{"id": ""}`.

quotes: Entitlements is one administrative entitlement record: a set of roles, the
Scope and Service are pointers because they are genuinely optional in the
response. A ZIAM-service entitlement carries no `scope` key at all, and as
value types the absence was indistinguishable from `{"id": ""}`

user-action-paths.summary: The contract writes the user actions as colon suffixes on the user path (`/users/{id}:setskipmfa`), while the Go SDK sends them as a further path segment after a slash.

positions.says: Skip MFA is POST /users/{id}:setskipmfa; reset and update password take the same colon form.

user-action-paths.impact: If the API routes only the colon form, every Go user action fails; a raw caller should follow the contract until a trace shows which form a tenant accepts.
